verdict.rationale: Aider has its own programmatic surfaces: a Python scripting interface (Coder.create / coder.run), a one-shot `--message` CLI mode, and command-line, config-file and environment-variable options. However, the vendor states the Python API is not officially supported or documented and may break without notice, and there is no HTTP API or spec. Nothing shows that every interactive feature (in-chat commands like /undo, /test, /architect, /voice, or the browser UI) is reachable programmatically. missing for 10: documented parity mapping each UI/in-chat command to an API equivalent, an officially supported and versioned API, an HTTP API or machine-readable spec, independent corroboration of full-feature programmatic use

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote:
# This will execute one instruction on those files and then return
coder.run("make a script that prints hello world")
Aider takes a `--message` argument, where you can give it a natural language instruction. It will do that one thing, apply the edits to the files and then exit.
Aider has many options which can be set with command line switches.
